messages:
emma: P1 customer reporting repeated mid-stream disconnects when switching from Wi‑Fi -> cellular. They see partial JSON chunks and get billed for tokens but client never receives final event. Repro on iOS 16.6 and Android 13. Example: they start a streaming chat, switch networks ~20s in, stream stops with no error.

marcus: Any logs from the client or server side yet? request_id or session id would help.

emma: Got a client debug dump and the request_id: rq_0b3c9f. Client shows TCP FIN from device then no graceful SSE close. App retries but gets a new stream; original billed as complete.

sam: Can you paste the proxied server logs around rq_0b3c9f? Curious about upstream 502/504 or TLS renegotiation.

emma: Pasting sanitized proxy tail (timestamps removed):
```
[proxy] accept conn from 10.1.2.3 -> proxy established
[proxy] upstream POST /v1/stream rq_0b3c9f token=REDACTED
[proxy] upstream response 200, streaming start
[proxy] network event: client FIN (abrupt)
[proxy] kept upstream connection open for 45s after client FIN
[proxy] upstream finally closed by server: 200 OK, connection reset
```

liam: Interesting — proxy kept upstream open after client FIN. That means our runtime finished the token generation and closed the response, but client already dropped. Is the billing system set to mark usage at upstream close rather than client ACK?

sam: Default pipeline marks tokens at finished response from model side. We do have a streaming partial-metering flag but it's opt-in. Could be why they got billed. Need to check why proxy didn't propagate FIN to upstream.

marcus: Customer is asking for a refund for the run and wants guidance to avoid future charges. Also wants reproducible steps for dev team.

liam: For traceroute: does app attempt TCP RST or just FIN then re-open? FIN indicates graceful close; RST indicates abort. If it's FIN, proxy should relay closure. If proxy ignores it (keepalive config) then upstream completes — billing mismatch.

sam: Quick repro to test: run curl with a streaming SSE endpoint then send SIGPIPE to mimic abrupt client close. Example:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"long"}' &
PID=$!
sleep 3; kill -9 $PID  # simulate client crash
```
Check runtime logs for whether model generation continued and whether the billing record closes on server finish.

marcus: I'll ask the customer to try this on their dev device and capture tcpdump. Also offered temporary credit for the invoice line while we triage.

emma: Customer provided tcpdump snippet (sanitized): shows 3-way close then new 3-way handshake 5s later. So they definitely tear then reconnect.

liam: Ok actionable items: 1) Sam to inspect proxy config to ensure FIN/RST are forwarded and not suppressed by idle timeouts. 2) Eng-runtime to add a defensive check: if client connection drops, abort upstream generation earlier (and mark as aborted for billing). 3) Support to offer credits + collect repro artifacts (tcpdump, exact SDK version).

sam: I can push a quick proxy tweak (set tcp_keepalive off for streaming routes, propagate RST) and run canary on staging. Will post PR link.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled to staging at 2025-09-11T18:30Z for proxy changes (canary=10%).

marcus: Customer accepted the temporary credit and will test the curl repro this afternoon, sending results.

emma: Adding SDK versions: iOS SDK 2.4.1, Android SDK 3.0.0-beta. Customer mentioned they use our default keepalive tweak in SDK (0 keepalive interval).

sam: Noted. If SDK forces keepalive, that could mask FIN semantics. Need to confirm whether our mobile SDKs send FIN proactively on network switch.

liam: I'll also add a billing flag to mark runs aborted by client disconnect so we can retroactively adjust if needed. Low-risk toggle.

marcus: Thanks — I'm looping in the account manager. Will update customer when we have staging canary results. :thumbsup:
